taxmill: PDF financial statements, milled into a dataset

Source: R/taxmill-package.R
taxmill-package.Rd

A financial statement is a table. It was a table when it was drawn up, and it is still a table when it arrives as a PDF – only now the structure is in the layout rather than in the file. taxmill is the route back: pull the text out of the PDF, shape the statement into simple space-delimited lines, and parse every file at once into one validated Excel workbook in tidy form.

Details

Tax accounts and ordinary annual accounts both work, because both are laid out as tables. That layout is the only thing the format relies on.

Everything stays on the machine

Nothing here touches the network. The documents this package is pointed at are usually confidential – a tax account is not a public annual report – so there is no upload, no API call, and no service to trust. accounts_pdf_to_txt() reads local PDFs and writes local text files; accounts_txt_to_xlsx() reads those and writes one workbook.

The three steps

library(taxmill)

accounts_pdf_to_txt("data/pdf", "data/txt")

# ... shape the statements into category and data lines by hand ...

accounts_txt_to_xlsx("data/txt", "data/accounts.xlsx", year = 2024)

The step in the middle is manual, and it is the slow one. That is not a gap waiting to be automated away: a PDF financial statement has no reliable machine-readable structure, the line labels differ between preparers, and a parser that guessed would produce numbers that look right and are wrong. Shaping the lines is the point at which a person decides what the table actually says. vignette("accounts") documents the format exactly.

What the package can do is make everything around that step cheap: extraction is one call, PDFs with no extractable text are skipped with a warning rather than silently, and validation problems are collected across all files and reported together at the end – so one malformed line in the twentieth file does not cost you nineteen files' worth of feedback.

If you do not have the PDFs yet

For published Danish annual reports, cvrr searches Erhvervsstyrelsens distribution service and downloads them; point accounts_pdf_to_txt() at the directory it filled. For a filing that exists as XBRL, use that instead – cvrr::read_xbrl() parses it with no manual step at all.

The functions

  • accounts_pdf_to_txt() – PDF financial statements to text files.

  • accounts_txt_to_xlsx() – shaped text files to one tidy Excel workbook, validated first.
